column1: # Claude's two passes (QUALITY.md end) for Mi Refugio: Reina-Valera 1909 only, natural US Latin American Spanish (tú/ustedes), RV1909 name spellings, one call and response 'Dios es bueno / todo el tiempo' at the story's turn.

column3: note
column5: note

column3: Faithful to Mark 4:35-41 (4:1 for the setting); Jesus's words only as RV1909 scripture; no promised calm for the listener, only the voice that can bring it.
column5: Plain, warm Spanish an abuela would read aloud; 'Dios es bueno / todo el tiempo' tied to the storm; the night's worries named without pity.

column3: Faithful to Exod 14 (vv5-9, 15-20, 23-28 told in words); God's command to Moses told, not voiced; the pillar of cloud as the text gives it.
column5: Families, elders and children in the crossing; the people's fear understood, not mocked.

column3: Faithful to Dan 6:1-23 (vv1-9 and 11-15, 17-18 told in words); Daniel's courage credited to God as v22-23.
column5: Daily prayer honoured; natural Spanish, no Spain-only forms.

column3: Faithful to Jonah 1-3 in RV1909 versification (the fish is RV1909 2:1, the prayer 2:2-10); Nineveh's repentance (3:5-10) told in words; second chances without a promise of outcome.
column5: Warm, plain; the sailors shown with respect.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 17 (vv4-31, 34-36, 38-44, 48, 52 told in words); RV1909 spelling Goliath; the battle credited to the LORD as v47.
column5: Giants named as everyday fears (debt, illness, loss) without promising they fall.

column3: Faithful to Gen 37:3-28 and 39:2; Reuben (v21-22) and the second dream (v9) told in words; Gen 50:20 echoed in our own words.
column5: Family wounds named gently; no blame beyond the text.

column3: Faithful to Luke 15:11-32; the father's words as RV1909 scripture; the open ending kept as Jesus left it.
column5: Natural Spanish for a family story; the elder brother also sought, not scorned.

column3: Faithful to Ruth 1 (vv1-7, 9-13, 15, 18-19 told in words); RV1909 spellings Noemi, Ruth, Orpha, Elimelech, Booz; David and Jesus from Ruth 4 and Matt 1, stated without references.
column5: Two widows shown with dignity; Naomi's bitterness honoured, not corrected.

column3: Faithful to Dan 3 (vv1-14, 19-23, 26-27 told in words); RV1909 spellings Sadrach, Mesach, Abed-nego, Nabucodonosor; 'y si no' as the heart (v18), no promise of rescue.
column5: Courage without bravado; plain Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Mark 5:25-34 (Jairus from v22 named for the setting); the purity law named plainly, not as an attack on Judaism; no promise of healing for the listener.
column5: The woman honoured, called 'hija' as Jesus called her; her shame and courage told with care.

column3: Faithful to Gen 7:1-5, 8:6-12, 9:12-16 (the family entering from 7:7, the altar from 8:20, told in words); God's covenant read only as RV1909; the closing names God's faithfulness, no promise of an outcome for the listener.
column5: Waiting named as the listener's real life (a noticia, una respuesta); plain warm Spanish; call and response tied to the open door of the ark.

column3: Faithful to Esth 4:1-17 and 5:1-3 (Amán's decree and Esther's orphan upbringing from chs 2-3, told in words); notes God is unnamed in the book without adding doctrine; Esther's fast credited to prayer and community, not to her courage alone.
column5: RV1909 spellings kept (Esther, Mardochêo, Amán); the fear honoured; no 'you were born for this' slogan pushed on the listener.

column3: Faithful to Job 1:13-22 and 42:10-17; says plainly the restored goods are not a promise or formula and the first children did not come back; lament allowed; points to iglesia and pastor for grief.
column5: Mourning customs explained with respect; would not wound a grieving mother; Spanish an abuela would read aloud.

column3: Faithful to Gen 1:1-5 and 26-31 (days 2-5 summarised in words); imago Dei stated for every person and every skin without an ethnicity claim; no sleep promise, only rest and the returning light.
column5: Dignity of every person made explicit and gentle; natural night-time close.

column3: Faithful to John 4:5-30 (vv16-18 and 27 told in words); Jesus's words only as scripture; her past named without shaming, as the text does; 'living water' not turned into a promise.
column5: The woman is never called by a slur or pity word; the barrier between Jews and Samaritans explained plainly; she is shown as the first messenger to her town.

column3: Faithful to Matt 14:22-33 (the feeding of 14:13-21 named as setting); the fourth watch explained correctly; 'Señor, sálvame' offered as a prayer, no promise of rescue from bills or diagnosis.
column5: Peter shown with respect (the only one who stepped out); everyday troubles named without stereotype.

column3: Faithful to Exod 3:1-14 (Moses's 40 years in Midian from Acts 7:30 and Exod 2, told in words); God never voiced, YO SOY read only as scripture; 'Yo estaré contigo' quoted as God's word to Moses, then applied as presence, not an outcome.
column5: An older man called by God: speaks to elders with dignity; the desert season named kindly.

column3: Faithful to Gen 45:1-15 and 50:19-21 (Jacob's death and the brothers' fear, 50:15-18, told in words); forgiveness not rushed, harm named as real, no pressure on a hurt listener to forgive tonight.
column5: Weeping men shown with dignity; family reconciliation in natural Spanish; would comfort someone carrying an old family wound.

column3: Faithful to Luke 10:38-42; Martha not condemned for serving, as Jesus does not; the mention of Martha's faith in John 11 is scripture, not invention; no ruling on women's roles (sitting at his feet explained as a disciple's place only).
column5: Martha's tiredness recognised (cooking, children, the parents we care for) without the 'busy woman' joke; tender 'Marta, Marta'.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kgs 17:8-16 (the brook of 17:3-7 named as setting); states plainly this is not a give-to-get rule (no prosperity reading); daily bread, not a full pantry.
column5: The widow shown with dignity and faith, not as a poverty picture; a foreign widow seen by God, natural Latin American Spanish.
